channel.title: The Awesome Ledger — awesome-raspberry-pi
channel.description: New entries across the GitHub awesome ecosystem, diffed nightly.

item.title: Rasptele — via awesome-raspberry-pi
item.description: Monitor Raspberry Pi health, manage Docker containers, and control Pi-hole through Telegram without exposing inbound ports.

item.title: CharlieBoard — via awesome-raspberry-pi
item.description: Open-source transit display using WS2812B LEDs with real-time vehicle tracking, geographically accurate PCB map, and a web control interface.

item.title: piscout — via awesome-raspberry-pi
item.description: Windows desktop app that scans the LAN for Raspberry Pis, opens an SSH terminal and remote desktop, shows temperature and load of several Pis, uploads files by drag and drop, and flashes SD cards.

item.title: nook — via awesome-raspberry-pi
item.description: Turns a Pi into a shared folder and a network drive on your tailnet, both driven from another machine over SSH, with the disk offered over iSCSI or NBD.

item.title: VoxRT — via awesome-raspberry-pi
item.description: On-device voice AI SDKs for Raspberry Pi, offering wake-word detection, VAD, keyword spotting, and streaming ASR, with a 100 KB wake-word model that runs at 5.3% CPU sustained on a Pi Zero 2 W.

item.title: Tiny Film Camera — via awesome-raspberry-pi
item.description: Open-source digital camera with physical controls, film-inspired looks, a 3D-printed enclosure, and a phone-friendly gallery. Supports Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W.

item.title: Raspberry Pi TV Simulator — via awesome-raspberry-pi
item.description: Simulates a channel change with random video playback on an old tube TV, switching between static noise and composite video.

item.title: MeshSat — via awesome-raspberry-pi
item.description: Off-grid messaging gateway that bridges Meshtastic LoRa, Iridium satellite, cellular SMS, APRS, ZigBee and BLE over a Reticulum routing layer, running as a Docker container on a Raspberry Pi.

item.title: Coffee Edition — via awesome-raspberry-pi
item.description: A two-page newspaper printed every morning by a Raspberry Pi Pico W or Pico 2 W, written overnight by a Claude Code routine, checked by GitHub Actions and streamed to a network printer over IPP.

item.title: Clock/Calendar Retrofit — via awesome-raspberry-pi
item.description: Retrofits a broken electronic clock/calendar with a Raspberry Pi Pico W, synced over Wi-Fi via NTP.

item.title: Cannvas — via awesome-raspberry-pi
item.description: Family touchscreen dashboard for a portrait TV with an infrared touch frame, with whiteboards, chores, calendar and Home Assistant controls, running on a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B.

item.title: Bad Thing of the Edge — via awesome-raspberry-pi
item.description: Mechanical gaming keyboard for the left hand, built around a Raspberry Pi Pico.

item.title: StickTime Pi — via awesome-raspberry-pi
item.description: Raspberry Pi 4 FPV drone simulator for analog goggles, composite out into a 5.8 GHz video transmitter, flown with a real RC radio over WiFi, USB or Bluetooth.

item.title: Philosopher — via awesome-raspberry-pi
item.description: A conversational-AI plush toy (Raspberry Pi + local LLM) that recognizes faces, reads emotions, remembers people, and talks with configurable personalities (100% local).

item.title: Orbit OS — via awesome-raspberry-pi
item.description: Android-like platform installed on top of Raspberry Pi OS: signed apps from an app store, atomic OTA updates, and Go, Python and Java SDKs to control GPIO, I²C, UART and the camera, with a VS Code extension (Orbit Studio) to run code live on the Pi and deploy in one click. Supports Raspberry Pi 3, 4, 5 and Zero 2 W.

item.title: EdgeLLM Bench — via awesome-raspberry-pi
item.description: Leaderboard of local LLM speeds (tokens/sec) on Raspberry Pi 5, 4 and CM4 compared with Jetson and RK3588 boards, each result linked to its source.

item.title: RelaySSH — via awesome-raspberry-pi
item.description: Hosted reverse SSH relay for Pis behind CGNAT or LTE, connect with plain ssh, no port forwarding or client software.

item.title: sbc.compare — via awesome-raspberry-pi
item.description: Benchmarks, specs and prices for 20+ Raspberry Pi models, from the Zero to the Pi 5 in every RAM size, all tested in-house with the same methodology, with side-by-side comparisons.
